capabilities.scope: Linux CO-RE loader, tracepoint attach, optional atomic Zenoh publish/callback and Linux raw-port syscall uprobe pairs, fixed event decode, privileged gateway, raw-port, synchronized process-leader-exit, controlled single-process cgroup-v2 OOM victim, controlled scheduler-migration, controlled scheduler-runqueue, controlled loopback NET_RX softirq, controlled virtual-veth unhandled-EtherType receive drop and controlled anonymous-page first-write page-fault host qualifications, bounded scheduler runqueue and tracked-TID migration evidence, bounded IRQ/softirq duration evidence with optional CPU/vector filtering, bounded EtherType/ifindex skb drop windows, bounded tracked-process page-fault windows, bounded cpufreq policy-limit episodes, bounded request-correlated gateway and per-thread raw-port syscall duration evidence, leader-thread process-exit filtering, OOM victim-PID attribution and incident correlation
capabilities.limitation: Hosted privileged Linux qualifies the gateway publish/callback and raw-port shared marker chains, one synchronized worker-suppression/leader-exit chain, one controlled single-process cgroup-v2 OOM victim-PID chain, one exact-TID two-CPU scheduler-migration threshold chain, one exact-TID controlled FIFO-contention wake-to-switch scheduler-runqueue chain, one CPU/vector-filtered loopback NET_RX softirq-duration chain, one isolated virtual-veth unhandled-EtherType receive-drop threshold chain, and one pinned-child 16-page anonymous first-write page-fault count-window chain through CO-RE verifier/load, real tracepoint or uprobe attachment, ringbuf decode, statistics, incident correlation and observer health projection. The network-drop evidence proves protocol and receive-ifindex filtering plus one hosted virtual protocol-stack drop path only; it does not qualify physical NICs, drivers, NAPI, XDP, qdisc, queue pressure, congestion, real EtherCAT devices or a production root cause. The OOM evidence proves one hosted leaf-cgroup memory.max injection, exact local oom_kill count, SIGKILL exit and raw mark_victim PID only; it does not resolve victim TGID, namespace/cgroup identity, trigger task, allocation, global pressure, delegated-container behavior or restart policy. The page-fault evidence proves one hosted x86_64 user-write/not-present error-code and count-threshold chain only; it does not expose address/IP, classify major/minor from BPF, measure handler duration, or qualify memory pressure, swap/storage, natural workload cause or product thresholds. The softirq evidence proves one controlled UDP GSO loopback execution only; it does not qualify hard IRQ, real NIC/driver/NAPI behavior, product interrupt budgets, sustained pressure or causal task ownership. Migration evidence proves controlled A-to-B-to-A movement and count-threshold correlation only; it does not prove migration cause, affinity-policy failure, measured stall latency or cache/NUMA impact. Runqueue evidence proves one injected wake-to-switch interval only; it does not qualify natural workload causes, ordinary scheduler behavior, product priorities or CPU isolation. Process-exit evidence contains no exit code/signal and does not prove complete thread-group death or restart supervision. Gateway evidence does not qualify a live Zenoh session, router/transport queue, IPC, serialization, permit or reconnect cause. Raw-port evidence does not qualify real AF_PACKET/NIC load or cycle/driver/NIC/wire/slave timing. Production target kernels, overhead/WCET, ROS2, recorder, natural-load runqueue root cause and hard-IRQ or production-NIC/sustained softirq pressure, physical-NIC/cpufreq-limit injection, global OOM behavior, portable page-fault semantics, major/minor fault attribution, OOM victim TGID/cgroup resolution and instantaneous-frequency/residency/cause qualification remain open
